title: {{NAME}} and the Hero with a Silver Horn
moral: Sometimes the most powerful thing you can offer is belief.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a deep indigo cape over a white suit with a silver star, indigo boots, and silver gauntlets — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The unicorn appeared in the city the day {{NAME}} failed his superhero assessment for the second time.

He had the cape. He had the training. He had the determination.

What he lacked, according to three assessors, was the specific power required to register as an official hero. His ability: perfect recall, which they considered useful but insufficient.

The unicorn was standing outside the assessment building when he emerged. It looked at him with deep amber eyes.

"You too?" he said.

pages.content:
Her name was Arc, she had a horn that could amplify any latent power threefold, and she had been looking for a suitable partner for two years.

"Every official hero already has more power than they need," she said. (She communicated in images and feelings that he translated to words with his perfect recall, each one exact.)

"The ones who need amplifying are the ones who aren't official yet."

"Me," said {{NAME}}.

"You," she confirmed. "Perfect recall, amplified threefold, becomes something much larger. Shall I show you?"

pages.content:
With Arc's amplification, {{NAME}}'s perfect recall became something extraordinary.

Not just memory: pattern recognition across every piece of information he had ever absorbed. He could look at a crisis situation and recall every similar scenario, every solution, every outcome from everything he'd ever read, heard, or experienced.

In his first real emergency (a multi-vehicle accident, blocked roads, two injured), he directed response vehicles along three routes nobody else had thought of, routes he recalled from a street map he'd glanced at two years ago.

Everyone was out in six minutes.

pages.content:
He went back to the assessment board with the rescue report.

The three assessors looked at it, then at Arc, who was standing in the corridor because she had decided the lobby ceiling was too low.

"Your ability hasn't changed," said the lead assessor carefully.

"The application of it has," said {{NAME}}. "With Arc, it becomes strategy. Recall plus pattern recognition at speed equals crisis navigation. That's useful."

Arc, in the corridor, made the sound of distant thunder that was her version of agreement.

They registered him. Official hero. Partner classification: unicorn.

pages.content:
He walked home in the evening with his official registration card in his pocket and Arc at his side, her horn occasionally illuminating the path ahead.

He thought about perfect recall, and how for years he had thought of it as a minor thing, not quite enough.

Not the power. The way it was used. The partner who believed it could be more.

He got into bed and Arc stood in the garden below his window, her horn a soft silver thread in the dark.

"Same time tomorrow?" he called.

The horn pulsed once: yes. See you then.
